evidence: Expected: secret-lifecycle documentation should state every destination and transmission of the client secret accurately.

Observed: README.md says the secret is sent over the loopback POST body to the local server and then “never anywhere else.” The implemented client-credentials flow necessarily sends that secret from the server to Microsoft's token endpoint initially and again during silent renewal.
This wording can cause users to misunderstand the external exposure and lifecycle of a high-value credential.
findings.remediation: Replace “never anywhere else” with precise wording: the browser sends the secret only to the loopback server; the server transmits it directly to Microsoft's tenant token endpoint for initial token acquisition and renewal, while never returning it to the browser or sending it to any non-Microsoft destination. Align docs/security-boundaries.md if necessary.
findings.title: Client-secret transmission documentation is materially inaccurate
findings.verification: Review the revised lifecycle text against auth.py's client-credentials request construction and renewal path, then rerun Markdown/governance validation.

evidence: Expected: the default manual workflow requires a recorded human issue-advance/start decision before beginning ISSUE-0011.
Observed: DECISION-020 explicitly says it “does not authorize starting ISSUE-0011” and that ISSUE-0011 does not start as part of that decision.

No later decision authorizing ISSUE-0011 was found. CURRENT.md instead asserts that the issue started because no deferral was recorded, which infers authorization contrary to the default-manual rule and the explicit exclusion.
findings.remediation: Stop progression and obtain an exact human decision on whether to authorize/ratify ISSUE-0011 and this candidate. Record that decision and reconcile CURRENT.md and the issue record without implying that absence of deferral grants approval. Any resulting relevant documentation change requires a fresh review.
findings.title: ISSUE-0011 lacks the required human start authorization
findings.verification: Confirm a committed human-authored decision explicitly binds ISSUE-0011's start and intended scope/candidate, and verify CURRENT.md links to it consistently.

limitations: The required test suite could not independently pass: 68 server tests were blocked by sandbox loopback restrictions.
The required py_compile check could not complete because the read-only checkout prevented bytecode output.
The required governance validator could not complete because the sandbox provided no writable temporary directory.
The documented non-live server walkthrough could not be independently repeated because the sandbox denies loopback socket binding.
The target commit is represented as a root commit in this isolated checkout, so ancestry to the supplied base could not be established; exact endpoint identities and their direct diff were verified.
No live tenant authentication was performed, as explicitly excluded by the approved issue.
review.summary: BLOCKED. The candidate has one material documentation defect: it incorrectly says the app-only secret is never sent anywhere beyond the local server, omitting transmission to Microsoft's token endpoint. More fundamentally, repository evidence contains no human authorization to start ISSUE-0011 and the latest decision explicitly excludes it. Independent required checks also could not complete in the read-only, no-loopback sandbox.
